# Camera sampling oracle

`campath-upstream.json` is generated by compiling `shared/AfxMath.cpp` from
advancedfx v2.191.1, commit `b97636852b8eecae09285b5a386192bb285638eb`.
It contains original synthetic camera paths, not game data.

```powershell
git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.191.1 https://github.com/advancedfx/advancedfx.git HLAE_SOURCE
python scripts/generate-campath-oracle.py HLAE_SOURCE crates/hlae/tests/fixtures/campath-upstream.json
cargo test --locked -p vibe-cs-hlae --test camera_sampling -- --nocapture
```

The generator requires `g++`; it removes the precompiled-header include and
defines MSVC's `abstract` annotation as empty. All upstream math bodies are
unchanged. C++ is used only to regenerate development fixtures, never at runtime.
The oracle covers nonuniform intervals, yaw wraparound, stationary orientation,
near-pole rotations, six-decimal XML knots, linear and spherical cubic modes.

Scalar interpolation solves the zero-endpoint-velocity C2 spline with Hermite
segments. Rotation follows HLAE's CC0 qspline variant, including its maximum of
three rate iterations (`do/while(iter++ < 2)`) and 1e-6 tolerance. Rust uses
per-shot coefficient storage and supports concurrent callers. See the MIT and
CC0 attribution files under `../../licenses/`.

This proves numerical parity with the pinned source; it does not substitute for
the roadmap's separate real `mirv_campath draw`/capture acceptance.
